classification.difficultyReason: Find two different triangular face heights using Pythagoras, sum all faces and the rectangular base, then calculate volume.

content.prompt: In the pyramid $VABCD$ shown, $VB$ is perpendicular to rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=12\text{ m}$, $BC=8\text{ m}$ and $VB=5\text{ m}$.

spec.description: Rectangular-based pyramid with V directly above B. Solid edges DC, CB, BV, VC and VD; dashed hidden edges DA, AB and AV. All five vertex labels retained. House style replaces ordinary source blue and red edge colours with black; hidden-edge meaning remains dashed. No shading.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a rectangle; VB is perpendicular to its plane. Numerical dimensions remain in the stem.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the surface area of the pyramid, in $\text{m}^2$, correct to one decimal place.

answer.short:
$254.6\text{ m}^2$

Use Pythagoras to find the face heights, then add the four triangular areas and the rectangular base.
answer.worked:
Since $VB$ is perpendicular to the base, triangles $VAB$ and $VBC$ are right-angled at $B$.

$$\begin{align*}VA&=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}\\VA&=13\text{ m}\\VC&=\sqrt{8^2+5^2}\\VC&=\sqrt{89}\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

As $AD\parallel BC$ and $DC\parallel AB$, the perpendicular face heights for triangles $VAD$ and $VDC$ are $VA$ and $VC$, respectively.

$$\begin{align*}A_{ABCD}&=12\times8=96\text{ m}^2\\A_{VAB}&=\tfrac12\times12\times5=30\text{ m}^2\\A_{VBC}&=\tfrac12\times8\times5=20\text{ m}^2\\A_{VAD}&=\tfrac12\times8\times13=52\text{ m}^2\\A_{VDC}&=\tfrac12\times12\times\sqrt{89}=6\sqrt{89}\text{ m}^2\\S&=96+30+20+52+6\sqrt{89}\\S&=198+6\sqrt{89}\\S&\approx254.6\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the volume of the pyramid.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height is $VB=5\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}V&=\tfrac13Ah\\V&=\tfrac13\times(12\times8)\times5\\V&=160\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$$
